grid.origin: top-left corner of the arena is (0, 0)
grid.x_axis: column index, increases to the right

agent.collision_shape: axis-aligned square box, half-width = collision_radius, around the capsule

spawn.heading: uniform random in [-pi, pi), drawn from the match seed

arena_rules.walkable_region: floor and mud together form one 4-connected region
arena_rules.spawn_possible: at least two non-mud floor cells at least min_separation apart

tournament.arena_source: locked generator seeded with the organizer's secret seed
tournament.pairing: one chaser file and one evader file

observation.offset_convention: dx = columns to the right, dy = rows downward, relative to the cell containing the agent's center

definitions.blk_dx_dy: block value of the cell at that offset (blk_0_0 is the cell the agent stands on)
definitions.move_x: displacement along x during the previous tick (after mud and collisions) / move_scale
definitions.move_y: displacement along y during the previous tick (after mud and collisions) / move_scale

tick_order: build both observations from the state at the start of the tick
both agents produce raw outputs; each is clamped to [-1, 1]
update both headings, wrapped to [-pi, pi)
compute each speed; mud is looked up at the cell containing the center at the start of the tick
move both agents along their new headings by speed * dt, one axis at a time (x, then y), stopping flush against any wall in the way (so agents slide along walls)
record each agent's actual displacement as next tick's move_x, move_y
if center distance <= tag radius the chaser wins and the match ends
if this was the last tick the evader wins

practice_opponents.omniscient_chaser: deterministic; shortest walking route around walls to the evader's true position, full thrust
practice_opponents.omniscient_evader: deterministic; walks to the open cell it can reach before the chaser that is farthest from the chaser, preferring open space
practice_opponents.baselines: baselines/baseline_chaser.json and baselines/baseline_evader.json, ordinary agent files
practice_opponents.interface: both scripted opponents act only through the standard action vector, so physics is identical to a trained agent

agent_file.weight_layout: for each layer in order: kernel W (n_in x units, row-major) then bias b (units). layer output = activation(x @ W + b)

fields: agents (name, role, color, x[], y[], heading[])

guarantees: no agent ever moves farther in one tick than speed * dt * terrain multiplier
no agent box ever overlaps a wall
